def make_client(sender_wallet: str) -> OpenPaymentsInterface:
    entry = get_key_for_wallet(sender_wallet)
    if entry is None:
        msg = f"No key registered for wallet '{sender_wallet}'. Call POST /keys/generate first."
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail=msg,
        )
    return OpenPaymentsInterface(
        key_id=entry["kid"],
        private_key_pem=entry["private_key_pem"],
        wallet_address=sender_wallet,
    )


def verify_interaction_hash(
    client_nonce: str,
    interact_nonce: str,
    interact_ref: str,
    auth_server: str,
    received_hash: str,
) -> bool:
    # Same as Rafiki: the grant URL goes in without a trailing slash (the SDK's HashManager adds one)
    data = f"{client_nonce}\n{interact_nonce}\n{interact_ref}\n{auth_server}"
    computed = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(data.encode()).digest()).decode()
    return hmac.compare_digest(computed, received_hash)


def count_periods(term_minutes: int, period_minutes: int) -> int:
    # Periods that start within the term; the last one may be partial
    return max(1, math.ceil(term_minutes / period_minutes))


def min_cap(debt: int, term_minutes: int, period_minutes: int) -> int:
    # Smallest cap per period that still lets the debt be repaid within the term
    return math.ceil(debt / count_periods(term_minutes, period_minutes))


def build_interval(start: datetime, term_minutes: int, period_minutes: int) -> str:
    # ISO 8601 repeating interval, e.g. R4/2026-10-17T05:00:00Z/P7D: the grant's cap resets
    # every period and the grant stops after the last period
    count = count_periods(term_minutes, period_minutes)
    period = f"P{period_minutes // 1440}D" if period_minutes % 1440 == 0 else f"PT{period_minutes}M"
    return f"R{count}/{start:%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ}/{period}"

@app.post("/loans")
def create_loan(req: CreateLoanRequest):
    if req.loan_id in loans:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409, detail=f"Loan '{req.loan_id}' already exists"
        )

    # The cap must let the debt be repaid within the term; default to the minimum
    minimum_cap = min_cap(int(req.amount_value), req.term_minutes, req.period_minutes)
    if req.weekly_cap_value is None:
        cap = minimum_cap
    elif int(req.weekly_cap_value) < minimum_cap:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail=f"Cap {req.weekly_cap_value} is too low: repaying {req.amount_value} in "
            f"{count_periods(req.term_minutes, req.period_minutes)} periods needs at least {minimum_cap}",
        )
    else:
        cap = int(req.weekly_cap_value)

    client = make_client(ABBO_WALLET_ADDRESS)
    borrower = client.discover_receiver_servers(req.borrower_wallet)
    lender = client.discover_receiver_servers(req.lender_wallet)

    start = datetime.now(UTC)
    term_end = start + timedelta(minutes=req.term_minutes)

    # 1. The loan's incoming payment on the lender's wallet: accepts at most the debt, until term_end
    incoming_token = client.request_incoming_payment_grant(req.lender_wallet)
    lender_incoming_url, _ = client.create_incoming_payment(
        receiver_wallet=req.lender_wallet,
        resource_server=lender["resource_server"],
        access_token=incoming_token,
        amount_value=req.amount_value,
        asset_code=lender["asset_code"],
        asset_scale=lender["asset_scale"],
        expires_at=term_end,
    )

    # 2. The capped permission on the borrower's wallet (approved once, interactively)
    nonce = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    interval = build_interval(start, req.term_minutes, req.period_minutes)
    redirect_url, pending_grant = client.request_loan_grant(
        borrower_wallet=req.borrower_wallet,
        lender_incoming_url=lender_incoming_url,
        cap_value=str(cap),
        interval=interval,
        asset_code=borrower["asset_code"],
        asset_scale=borrower["asset_scale"],
        finish_uri=f"{CALLBACK_BASE_URL}/loan/{req.loan_id}",
        nonce=nonce,
    )

    loans[req.loan_id] = {
        "borrower_wallet": req.borrower_wallet,
        "lender_wallet": req.lender_wallet,
        "borrower_auth_server": borrower["auth_server"],
        "lender_auth_server": lender["auth_server"],
        "lender_incoming_url": lender_incoming_url,
        "asset_code": borrower["asset_code"],
        "asset_scale": borrower["asset_scale"],
        "debt": req.amount_value,
        "balance": req.amount_value,
        "weekly_cap": str(cap),
        "min_cap": str(minimum_cap),
        "interval": interval,
        "term_start": start.isoformat(),
        "term_end": term_end.isoformat(),
        "nonce": nonce,
        "pending_grant": pending_grant,
        "status": "waiting_approval",
    }
    return {
        "loan_id": req.loan_id,
        "approve_url": str(redirect_url),
        "lender_incoming_url": lender_incoming_url,
        "term_end": term_end.isoformat(),
        "cap_per_period": str(cap),
        "min_cap": str(minimum_cap),
        "interval": interval,
    }


@app.get("/callback/loan/{loan_id}")
def loan_callback(loan_id: str, interact_ref: str = Query(...), hash: str = Query(...)):
    loan = loans.get(loan_id)
    if loan is None or loan["status"] != "waiting_approval":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404, detail=f"No loan waiting approval: '{loan_id}'"
        )

    # Check that this redirect really comes from the borrower's wallet
    valid = verify_interaction_hash(
        loan["nonce"],
        loan["pending_grant"].root.interact.finish,
        interact_ref,
        loan["borrower_auth_server"],
        hash,
    )
    if not valid:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid interaction hash")

    client = make_client(ABBO_WALLET_ADDRESS)
    loan.update(client.continue_loan_grant(loan.pop("pending_grant"), interact_ref))
    loan["status"] = "active"
    return {"loan_id": loan_id, "status": "active", "term_end": loan["term_end"]}


@app.post("/loans/{loan_id}/disburse")
def disburse_loan(loan_id: str):
    loan = loans.get(loan_id)
    if loan is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Loan '{loan_id}' not found")
    # The borrower must approve the repayment grant before the lender releases the money.
    # "disbursing" is allowed so the lender can get a fresh approval link.
    if loan["status"] not in ("active", "disbursing"):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409,
            detail=f"Loan '{loan_id}' is '{loan['status']}': it can be disbursed only when 'active'",
        )

    # One-off payment from the lender's wallet to the borrower's wallet; the lender approves it.
    # The amount lands in the borrower's currency, so this assumes both wallets share a currency.
    client = make_client(ABBO_WALLET_ADDRESS)
    redirect_url, outgoing_grant, lender_resource_server, nonce, quote_id = (
        client.create_payment_request(
            receiver_wallet=loan["borrower_wallet"],
            amount_value=loan["debt"],
            order_id=loan_id,
            callback_base_url=f"{CALLBACK_BASE_URL}/disburse",
            sender_wallet=loan["lender_wallet"],
        )
    )

    loan["pending_disbursement"] = {
        "outgoing_grant": outgoing_grant,
        "lender_resource_server": lender_resource_server,
        "nonce": nonce,
        "quote_id": quote_id,
    }
    loan["status"] = "disbursing"
    return {"loan_id": loan_id, "approve_url": str(redirect_url), "status": "disbursing"}


@app.get("/callback/disburse/{loan_id}")
def disburse_callback(loan_id: str, interact_ref: str = Query(...), hash: str = Query(...)):
    loan = loans.get(loan_id)
    if loan is None or loan["status"] != "disbursing":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404, detail=f"No loan waiting for disbursement: '{loan_id}'"
        )
    pending = loan["pending_disbursement"]

    # Check that this redirect really comes from the lender's wallet
    valid = verify_interaction_hash(
        pending["nonce"],
        pending["outgoing_grant"].root.interact.finish,
        interact_ref,
        loan["lender_auth_server"],
        hash,
    )
    if not valid:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid interaction hash")

    client = make_client(ABBO_WALLET_ADDRESS)
    outgoing_token = client.continue_outgoing_payment_grant(
        outgoing_grant=pending["outgoing_grant"],
        interact_ref=interact_ref,
    )
    payment_id = client.create_outgoing_payment(
        resource_server=pending["lender_resource_server"],
        outgoing_token=outgoing_token,
        quote_id=pending["quote_id"],
        sender_wallet=loan["lender_wallet"],
    )

    loan.pop("pending_disbursement")
    loan["disbursement_payment_id"] = str(payment_id)
    loan["disbursed_at"] = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    loan["status"] = "disbursed"
    return {"loan_id": loan_id, "status": "disbursed", "payment_id": str(payment_id)}


@app.get("/loans/{loan_id}")
def get_loan(loan_id: str):
    loan = loans.get(loan_id)
    if loan is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Loan '{loan_id}' not found")
    hidden = {
        "pending_grant",
        "pending_disbursement",
        "nonce",
        "access_token",
        "manage_url",
        "continue_token",
    }
    return {"loan_id": loan_id, **{k: v for k, v in loan.items() if k not in hidden}}

    def create_outgoing_payment(
        self,
        resource_server: str,
        outgoing_token: str,
        quote_id: str,
        sender_wallet: str,
    ):
        payment = OutgoingPaymentRequestWithQuote.model_construct(
            walletAddress=WalletAddress.model_validate(
                sender_wallet
            ),
            quoteId=quote_id,
        )
        print(
            "Outgoing payment body:",
            payment.model_dump(exclude_unset=True, mode="json"),
        )
        try:
            outgoing = self.client.outgoing_payments.post_create_payment(
                payment=payment,
                resource_server_endpoint=resource_server,
                access_token=outgoing_token,
            )
        except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
            print("Outgoing payment error response:", e.response.text)
            raise
        return outgoing.id

    def create_payment_request(
        self,
        receiver_wallet: str,
        amount_value: str,
        order_id: str,
        callback_base_url: str,
        sender_wallet: str
    ):
        nonce = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
        finish_uri = f"{callback_base_url}/{order_id}"
        print(f"[make_payment] finish_uri = {finish_uri}")

        access_token = self.request_incoming_payment_grant(receiver_wallet)

        receiver_info = self.discover_receiver_servers(receiver_wallet)
        incoming_payment_url, _ = self.create_incoming_payment(
            receiver_wallet=receiver_wallet,
            resource_server=receiver_info["resource_server"],
            access_token=access_token,
            amount_value=amount_value,
            asset_code=receiver_info["asset_code"],
            asset_scale=receiver_info["asset_scale"],
        )

        sender_info = self.discover_receiver_servers(sender_wallet)
        quote_token = self.request_quote_grant(sender_wallet)
        quote = self.create_quote(
            resource_server=sender_info["resource_server"],
            access_token=quote_token,
            incoming_payment_url=incoming_payment_url,
            sender_wallet=sender_wallet,
        )

        redirect_url, outgoing_grant = self.request_outgoing_payment_grant(
            incoming_payment_url=incoming_payment_url,
            finish_uri=finish_uri,
            nonce=nonce,
            amount_value=str(quote.debitAmount.value),
            asset_code=str(quote.debitAmount.assetCode.root),
            asset_scale=int(quote.debitAmount.assetScale.root),
            sender_wallet=sender_wallet
        )

        return (
            redirect_url,
            outgoing_grant,
            sender_info["resource_server"],
            nonce,
            str(quote.id),
        )

content.text:
The repayment endpoint is built. I tested it locally with a fake wallet, but haven't run it on the test network. Nothing is committed.

## `POST /loans/{loan_id}/sales`

Body: `{"sale_id": "nequi-001", "amount_value": "4500000"}`, in the tendero's minor units.

1. **It only runs on a `disbursed` loan.** Otherwise it returns 409.
2. **A `sale_id` that's already been processed** returns `duplicate` and pays nothing.
3. **Deduction = 10% of the sale, at most the remaining balance.** If that's 0, it returns `nothing_to_pay`.
4. **It pays through the new `pay_with_grant`** in `open_payment.py`:
   - quote from the tendero's wallet with `debitAmount` = the deduction;
   - outgoing payment with the token the tendero approved in `loan_callback`.

   There's no redirect.
5. **The balance drops by what the bank received** (`receiveAmount`), and the repayment is recorded on the loan under `repayments`. At 0 the loan becomes `paid_off`.
6. **If the wallet rejects the payment,** for example because this period's cap is used up, it returns **502** with the wallet's message. The balance and the repayment list stay unchanged.

## Kept simple on purpose

- **No cap counter in the app.** The tendero's wallet already enforces the per-period cap, and a payment over it comes back as the 502.
- **The rate is a constant,** `REPAYMENT_RATE_PERCENT = 10` in `app.py`, not a loan setting.
- **No token rotation and no carrying small amounts** to the next sale. Both stay in `NOTES_LATER.md` until a test shows you need them.

## What I tested (wallet calls faked)

- 409 before the loan is disbursed.
- A COP 45.00 sale pays 4.50.
- A resent sale returns `duplicate`.
- A tiny sale returns `nothing_to_pay`.
- A sale bigger than the balance is capped at the balance.
- A rejected payment returns 502 and leaves the balance unchanged.

Ruff reports nothing new: I applied its import formatting to `app.py`, and the remaining warnings were already there. The change is logged in `USAGE_AI.md`.

## Watch for on the test network

- **Fees can leave a small remainder.** The balance drops by what the bank receives. If fees make that less than the deduction, the last few units stay unpaid until the next sale. With two same-currency test wallets there are probably no fees, so check the first real repayment's `deduction` against its `received`.
- **The token expires.** If repayments start failing with 401 after a while, the token from `loan_callback` has expired (`expires_in` is on the loan), and you'll need the rotation from `NOTES_LATER.md`.

To test: create a loan, approve as the tendero, disburse and approve as the bank, then call `/sales`. Use a sale big enough to exceed the cap in one period to see the 502.

content.text:
Your logs alone don't show where the money stopped, so check two things. Creating an outgoing payment only means the tendero's wallet accepted the request. The money can still fail or be held afterwards.

## 1. Did the bank's loan incoming payment receive anything?

The incoming payment URL answers without authentication, so you can check it from the terminal. Take `lender_incoming_url` from `GET /loans/{loan_id}`:

```bash
curl -s -H "Accept: application/json" "<lender_incoming_url>"
```

Look at `receivedAmount`:
- **It went up:** the money did arrive. Look at the **bank** account in the test wallet UI. The loan pays into the incoming payment on `lender_wallet`. If the bank's test-wallet account has several wallet addresses or accounts, the balance appears on the account that owns that address.
- **It's still 0:** the payment didn't settle, so go to step 2.

## 2. What state is the outgoing payment in?

In your debugger, after a `/sales` call returns, evaluate this in the debug console with the loan's values:

```python
c = make_client(ABBO_WALLET_ADDRESS)
rs = c.discover_receiver_servers(loan["borrower_wallet"])["resource_server"]
op = c.client.outgoing_payments.get_outgoing_payment(
    payment_id=payment_id.rsplit("/", 1)[-1],
    resource_server_endpoint=rs.rstrip("/"),
    access_token=loan["access_token"],
)
print(op.failed, op.debitAmount, op.sentAmount)
```

- **`failed: True`:** the payment was attempted and rejected. Usual causes:
  - the incoming payment had expired (next section);
  - the tendero's wallet didn't have enough funds;
  - the incoming payment was already full.
- **`sentAmount` = 0 and not failed:** the payment is still being processed, or the wallet never funded it. Wait a few seconds and read it again.
- **`sentAmount` > 0:** it was sent, so step 1 should show it. Re-check which bank account you're looking at.

## The most likely cause if you're testing quickly

`create_loan` sets the bank's incoming payment to expire at `term_end`. If you created the loan with a short `term_minutes` (5 or 15), the incoming payment has probably expired by the time you've approved, disbursed and sent a sale. Payments to an expired incoming payment don't arrive. Compare `term_end` from `GET /loans/{loan_id}` with the time of your sale. If that's the problem, use a longer `term_minutes` with a short `period_minutes` (for example a 60-minute term with 5-minute periods), so you can still watch the cap reset.

Send me the `curl` output and the `failed`/`sentAmount` values, and I'll tell you which case it is.

The prints are in. Restart uvicorn, run one sale through `POST /loans/{loan_id}/sales`, and paste me the terminal lines that start with `[sale]`, `[pay]` and `[check]`.

**What each line shows:**

| Prefix | Where | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `[sale]` | `record_sale`, before paying | Sale amount and deduction, the tendero's wallet and currency, the bank's incoming payment URL, **the current time next to `term_end`**, the interval, and how long the token lasts (`token_expires_in`) |
| `[pay]` | `pay_with_grant` | The quote (where it pays to, debit and receive amounts, when it expires), then the ID of the outgoing payment created |
| `[sale] wallet rejected` | when the wallet refuses | The wallet's status code and error message |
| `[check]` | 3 seconds after paying | The outgoing payment (`failed`, `sent`, `receive`), and the bank's incoming payment as seen publicly, including its `receivedAmount` and whether it has completed or expired |

`debug_payment_status` is a new helper in `open_payment.py` that reads both ends of the payment. The 3-second wait is so the payment has time to settle before it reads them. Every new line is marked `# DEBUG`, so they're easy to find and remove once the issue is fixed.

**Checks:** the app imports, and every field the prints use exists in the SDK models. Ruff reports nothing new. I logged the change in `USAGE_AI.md` as temporary.

**Before you paste:** the output includes wallet addresses and payment URLs from the test network. Those are fine to share here. No tokens or keys are printed.

content.text:
The repayment reached the bank. Your prints show it at both ends:

```
[check] outgoing failed=False debit=8000000 sent=8000000 receive=8000000
[check] lender incoming payment: receivedAmount = 8000000 COP/2   ← COP 80,000 arrived
```

So the problem isn't the payment. It's when the test wallet credits the money to the bank's balance.

## Why the balance doesn't show it (very likely)

The test wallet runs on Rafiki. In Rafiki, money that arrives at an incoming payment isn't credited to the account balance as it arrives: the wallet provider moves it into the user's balance when the incoming payment **completes** (receives its full `incomingAmount`) or **expires**.

That fits both of your payments:

| Payment | Incoming payment | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Disbursement | `incomingAmount` = exactly the loan, so the payment fills it and it completes | ✅ shows in the tendero's balance |
| Repayment | the loan's incoming payment, `incomingAmount` = COP 1,000,000, has received COP 80,000 | ⏳ still open: not credited until it's full or expires at **06:35 UTC** |

**To confirm:** leave it until after 06:35 UTC, when the incoming payment expires, and check the bank's balance. If COP 80,000 appears then, that's the cause. I'm confident about how Rafiki handles this, but I haven't seen the test wallet's own code, so this is the check that settles it.

## What to change: your call

| Option | How | You get | You lose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. One incoming payment per repayment** | In `/sales`, create an incoming payment on the bank for exactly the deduction, then pay it | The bank's balance goes up on every sale, live in the demo | The grant's `receiver` limit. It can only name one incoming payment, so the grant would allow payments anywhere, up to the cap. The total debt limit would then be enforced only by the app. |
| **B. Keep one incoming payment per loan** | No code change | The strongest protection: only this loan, and never more than the debt | The bank sees the money only when the loan is fully paid or the term ends. During the demo, show progress from `receivedAmount`, which your `[check]` line already reads. |
| **C. One incoming payment per period** | A new incoming payment each week, and a new grant to match | A balance update each period | A new approval from the tendero each period. That defeats "approve once". |

**For the hackathon I'd keep B and show `receivedAmount` on the dashboard** as "the bank's wallet has received COP 80,000 of 1,000,000". That's the "ledger matches the rails" moment from your pitch doc. It keeps the best trust story, "her wallet only lets money go to this loan", which is worth more to the judges than a live balance change. Choose A if seeing the bank's balance move on stage matters more to you.

**Other details from the log:**
- **The pydantic `UserWarning`s are harmless.** They come from `model_construct`, which we use on purpose, and the request bodies are correct.
- **`token_expires_in=600`:** the tendero's token lasts 10 minutes. Sales more than 10 minutes after `loan_callback` will start failing with 401 until token rotation is built.

Tell me which option you want and I'll make the change. The debug prints can stay until then.

from open_payments_sdk.models.resource import (
    Amount,
    IncomingPayment,
    IncomingPaymentRequest,
    OutgoingPayment,
    OutgoingPaymentRequestWithQuote,
    PaginatedIncomingPayments,
    Pagination,
    PaymentListQuery,
    QuoteRequestBase,
    WalletAddress,
)

from models import IncomingPaymentInfo

from .helper import (
    compute_loan_payment,
    filter_by_completed,
    filter_by_date,
    get_info_from_incoming_payment,
    get_last_date,
    load_last_date,
    save_last_date,
)

IncomingPayment.__annotations__["updatedAt"] = Optional[datetime]
IncomingPayment.model_fields["updatedAt"].default = None
IncomingPayment.model_rebuild(force=True)

OutgoingPayment.__annotations__["updatedAt"] = Optional[datetime]
OutgoingPayment.model_fields["updatedAt"].default = None
OutgoingPayment.model_config["extra"] = "ignore"
OutgoingPayment.model_rebuild(force=True)

for _field in ("startCursor", "endCursor", "hasNextPage", "hasPrevPage"):
    Pagination.model_fields[_field].default = None
Pagination.model_rebuild(force=True)
PaginatedIncomingPayments.model_rebuild(force=True)

PaymentListQuery.model_fields["walletAddress"].serialization_alias = "wallet-address"
PaymentListQuery.model_config["serialize_by_alias"] = True
PaymentListQuery.model_rebuild(force=True)


    def request_list_incoming_payments_grant(
        self, wallet_address: str, finish_uri: str, nonce: str
    ):
        auth_server = self.discover_receiver_servers(wallet_address)["auth_server"]
        grant_req = GrantRequest(
            **{
                "access_token": {
                    "access": [
                        {
                            "type": "incoming-payment",
                            "actions": ["list-all", "read-all"],
                            "identifier": wallet_address,
                        }
                    ]
                },
                "client": self.client.client_wallet_address,
                "interact": {
                    "start": ["redirect"],
                    "finish": {
                        "method": "redirect",
                        "uri": finish_uri,
                        "nonce": nonce,
                    },
                },
            }
        )
        try:
            grant = self.client.grants.post_grant_request(grant_req, auth_server)
        except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
            print("List incoming payments grant error response:", e.response.text)
            raise
        return grant.root.interact.redirect, grant

    def get_incoming_payments(
        self,
        wallet_address: str,
        access_token: str,
        page_size: int = 1,
        fetch_all: bool = True,
    ) -> list[IncomingPaymentInfo]:
        resource_server = self.discover_receiver_servers(wallet_address)["resource_server"]

        payments: list[IncomingPaymentInfo] = []
        last_date = load_last_date()
        cursor = None
        while True:
            query_fields = {
                "walletAddress": WalletAddress.model_validate(wallet_address),
                "first": page_size,
            }
            if cursor:
                query_fields["cursor"] = cursor
            query = PaymentListQuery.model_construct(**query_fields)
            try:
                page = self.client.incoming_payments.get_incoming_payments(
                    query=query,
                    resource_server_endpoint=resource_server,
                    access_token=access_token,
                )
            except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
                print("List incoming payments error response:", e.response.text)
                raise
            formatted_payments = [
                get_info_from_incoming_payment(payment) for payment in page.result
            ]
            completed_payments = filter_by_completed(formatted_payments)
            filtered_payments = (
                filter_by_date(completed_payments, last_date) if last_date else completed_payments
            )
            payments.extend(filtered_payments)

            if (
                not fetch_all
                or not filtered_payments
                or not page.pagination.hasNextPage
                or not page.pagination.endCursor
            ):
                break

            cursor = page.pagination.endCursor

        last_date = get_last_date(payments) if payments else None
        if last_date:
            save_last_date(last_date)
        print(f"Retrieved {len(payments)} incoming payments. Last date: {last_date}")
        return payments

    def list_incoming_payments_with_loan(
        self,
        wallet_address: str,
        access_token: str,
        page_size: int = 1,
        fetch_all: bool = True,
        percentage_to_pay_loan: Decimal | None = None,
    ) -> list[IncomingPaymentInfo]:
        payments = self.get_incoming_payments(
            wallet_address,
            access_token,
            page_size,
            fetch_all,
        )
        payments_with_loans = [
            compute_loan_payment(payment, percentage_to_pay_loan) for payment in payments
        ]
        return payments_with_loans

+**What we're building:** **Abbo**, a sales-based microloan app for tiendas de barrio (concept doc: `docs/Hackaton/cuota-viva-hackathon-mvp.md`, written under the old working name Cuota Viva). A share of each digital sale repays the tendero's loan to the bank over ILP, within a daily cap the tendero approves once in their own wallet.

+**Roles:** Abbo is the Open Payments client (its own wallet `https://ilp.interledger-test.dev/abbo` and the only developer key). The tendero's wallet pays and the bank's wallet receives. Neither needs a key.
- [ ] **Day 2 PM:** demo script, Google Slides submission, final `USAGE_AI.md` pass

content.text:
I merged `main` into `obba-client`. The conflicts are resolved and staged, but I haven't committed. The two new pieces are tested locally against a fake wallet, not yet on the test network.

## How the pieces fit

1. **One approval from the tendero covers both.** `request_loan_grant` now asks the tendero's wallet for two kinds of access in the same grant: the capped outgoing payments, as before, plus `incoming-payment` with `list-all` and `read-all`. The token from `loan_callback` is used for both, so the tendero still approves only once.
2. **`POST /loans/{loan_id}/sync-sales` (new):**
   - It lists the tendero's incoming payments with the loan's token.
   - It keeps those that are **completed** and were **created after `disbursed_at`**. That leaves out older sales and the loan disbursement itself.
   - It repays from each one, oldest first, using the incoming payment's URL as the `sale_id`.
   - Running it again is safe: sales already repaid come back as `duplicate`. A sale the wallet rejects (for example, cap reached) is returned as `failed` and isn't recorded, so the next sync retries it.
3. **The sale logic now lives in one place.** `repay_from_sale` is used by both `/sales` (manual) and `/sync-sales`. `get_disbursed_loan` holds the shared checks.
4. **`list_incoming_payments`** in `open_payment.py` reads every page. I kept main's patches to `Pagination` and `PaymentListQuery`, because the list call needs them.

## What I removed from main, and why

| From main | Replaced by |
|---|---|
| `GET /payments/list/incoming` + `/callback/list-incoming/{id}` (their own grant and approval) | the loan grant, plus `/sync-sales` |
| `helper.py`, `checkpoint.json` (last-read date in a file) | the `disbursed_at` filter, plus sale IDs to skip duplicates. A shared checkpoint file would also mix up loans. |
| `IncomingPaymentInfo` and the Decimal 5% calculation | `repay_from_sale` (10%, integer minor units) |
| main's version of `/payments/initiate` and `/keys/generate` | kept commented out, as on your branch. Main's version wouldn't run against the current `create_payment_request`. |

It's all still in git history. Tell your teammate who wrote the listing, since their endpoints are gone from this branch.

I kept main's `demo/` pages, the ruff dev dependency in `pyproject.toml`, and both teams' `USAGE_AI.md` rows. I logged this merge there too.

## What I tested

- The grant request now contains both kinds of access, in a form the SDK accepts.
- A page of incoming payments with no `updatedAt` and no cursors parses correctly.
- `sync-sales`:
  - it skips a sale from before the disbursement and an incoming payment that isn't completed;
  - it repays two new sales at 10% each;
  - a second sync returns both as `duplicate`.
- `/sales` still works.

Ruff reports nothing new.

## Test on the test network before committing

1. **Make a new loan,** because older loans' grants don't include the listing access. Check that the tendero's approval screen accepts a grant that mixes the two access types. I haven't confirmed the test wallet allows it.
2. **After disbursing,** pay the tendero from a third ("customer") wallet, then call `/sync-sales`.
3. **Do it within 10 minutes of approving.** The listing uses the same 10-minute token, so after that you'll get a 502 "Could not read the borrower's payments" until token rotation is built.

To finish the merge once it works: `git commit`.

message.content: In the function sync_sales how the app knows which incoming transaction is already processed?

content.text:
Through the `sale_id`. `sync_sales` itself keeps no list of what it has read. It relies on the check inside `repay_from_sale`:

1. Each incoming payment's URL becomes the `sale_id`: `repay_from_sale(loan, str(sale.id), …)`.
2. When a repayment succeeds, `repay_from_sale` adds `{"sale_id": …, …}` to `loan["repayments"]`.
3. Before paying, it checks whether that `sale_id` is already in the list:
   ```python
   if any(r["sale_id"] == sale_id for r in repayments):
       return {"status": "duplicate", ...}
   ```

So every sync reads **all** the tendero's incoming payments again and skips the ones already in `loan["repayments"]`.

**Consequences:**
- **Only successful repayments are remembered.** If the wallet rejects a sale (cap reached) or the deduction is 0, nothing is recorded, so the next sync tries it again. That's deliberate for the cap: the sale gets repaid once the period resets.
- **A sale too small to deduct anything gets re-checked on every sync.** It costs no payment, just a quick check each time.
- **The memory lives in `loans`, in RAM.** If uvicorn restarts, the loan is gone along with its `repayments`, so nothing can be paid twice, but the loan has to be recreated.
- **Each sync reads every page.** That's fine for a demo. With hundreds of sales per loan you'd only read payments newer than the last one processed, which is what main's checkpoint did.

message.content: Is it making sure that the payment is completed?

content.text:
For the incoming sales, yes. For the tendero's repayment to the bank, no.

**Incoming sales: yes.** `sync_sales` only keeps incoming payments with `completed == True`:
```python
p for p in incoming if p.completed and p.createdAt > disbursed_at
```
An incoming payment that has received only part of its amount is skipped until it completes. That matches how the wallet credits money: only on completion.

**Repayment to the bank: no.** `repay_from_sale` marks the sale as repaid as soon as the tendero's wallet **accepts** the outgoing payment. It doesn't wait for the money to arrive. Two consequences:
- **If the payment fails after being accepted,** for example during ILP delivery, the sale is still recorded as repaid. It won't be retried, and the balance has already gone down.
- **The balance uses the quote's `receiveAmount`,** which is the amount promised, not what was actually delivered.

In your test run, the payment had fully arrived 3 seconds later (`failed=False`, `sent=8000000`, and the bank's `receivedAmount` matched). So on the test network this is unlikely to matter.

**If you want it confirmed:**
1. After creating the outgoing payment, read it back. Your earlier `debug_payment_status` did exactly that.
2. If `failed` is true, don't record the repayment, so the next sync retries the sale.
3. Use `sentAmount` or the bank's `receivedAmount` instead of the quote's figure.

That costs one extra call per sale and a short wait. Following YAGNI, I'd add it only if you ever see a repayment that doesn't arrive. For the demo, showing the bank's incoming payment `receivedAmount` next to your balance already proves they match.

message.content: Can the endpoint be executed by the UI when implemented every 10 seconds and identify the new sales and execute the payment?

content.text:
Yes, that works. Calling `/sync-sales` every 10 seconds finds new sales and pays them, and sales it has already paid are skipped. But there's one risk to handle first.

## Two syncs running at once can pay the same sale twice

`repay_from_sale` checks for duplicates **before** paying, but only records the sale **after** the payment returns. A sync takes a few seconds per new sale: it lists, then gets a quote grant, a quote and an outgoing payment. FastAPI runs these endpoints in parallel threads. So if a sync is still running when the next one starts, both can see the same sale as new, and both pay it.

That happens if:
- the UI uses `setInterval` and a sync takes longer than 10 seconds;
- two browser tabs (or two phones in the demo) are polling the same loan.

**The fixes, both small:**
1. **UI:** schedule the next call only after the previous one finishes, instead of firing every 10 seconds regardless:
   ```js
   async function poll() {
     try { await fetch(`/loans/${id}/sync-sales`, { method: "POST" }); }
     finally { setTimeout(poll, 10000); }
   }
   ```
2. **Server:** a lock per loan in `sync_sales`, so a second call waits until the first one finishes. That's about four lines with `threading.Lock`, and it also covers the multi-tab case.

I'd do both. The UI change alone doesn't protect you from a second tab.

## Two other things that will show up

- **After 10 minutes, every poll returns 502.** The tendero's token expires (`expires_in=600`), and listing and paying both use it. For a demo shorter than 10 minutes that's fine. For anything longer, you need the token rotation from `NOTES_LATER.md`.
- **Repeated rejections are expected.** When the period's cap is used up, each poll retries the same sales and gets `failed` until the cap resets. The response explains each one, so show "cap reached" in the UI instead of an error.

Want me to add the per-loan lock?

content: We're building Abbo, your Open Payments loan app, and just added automatic sale syncing so each tendero sale repays the bank. Next: decide whether I add a per-loan lock so 10-second polling can't pay a sale twice.

* Loan amount (*Monto a prestar*)
* Interest rate (*Tasa de interés*)
* Percentage deducted from each incoming sale/transaction (*Porcentaje de cada venta cobrado*)


2. Display the total repayment calculation (principal + interest) before submitting.
3. Submit button labeled `"Enviar al deudor"`.
4. Loan status panel tracking the state:
Terms sent → Approved/Rejected → Grant approved → Disbursement completed → Collections received (itemized list with date and amount) → Outstanding balance.

---

## Borrower UI (`deudor.html`)

*(Ensure all displayed text and labels are in Spanish)*

1. When terms are received, display them on screen with *Aprobar* and *Rechazar* action buttons.
2. If rejected, notify the lender UI and terminate the flow.
3. If approved, proceed with the grant workflow detailed below.
4. Status panel tracking: Grant status, disbursement received, collections made, remaining balance, and total amount collected during the current week.

---

## Complete Workflow

1. **Lender** defines and submits the loan terms.
2. **Borrower** views the terms and either approves or rejects them.
3. Upon approval, create the following grants using their respective endpoints:
* A debit grant on the borrower's account with a maximum limit equal to `principal + interest`.
* A read grant for all transactions on the borrower's account.


4. The **borrower** approves the grant via redirection to an authorization URL within their own UI.
5. Once the grant is approved, execute the disbursement from lender to borrower:
* Call the corresponding endpoint to create debit authorization on the lender's account.
* Redirect to the approval link *within the same lender UI tab* (do not open a new tab).
* Upon return via the callback URL, finalize the payment and reflect the updated status across both UIs.


6. **Automatic collection:** After disbursement, invoke the `sync-sales` endpoint.

---

## Deliverables

* Fully functional `prestador.html` and `deudor.html` files with complete Spanish UIs.
* A visible in-browser log panel on each UI showing API calls (endpoint, HTTP status, and summarized response payload) for debugging.
* Brief instructions explaining how to run and test the complete end-to-end flow.
* Minimize new endpoint creation; prioritize reusing existing, predefined endpoints.

@app.post("/loans")
def create_loan(req: CreateLoanRequest):
    if req.loan_id in loans:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409, detail=f"Loan '{req.loan_id}' already exists"
        )

    # The cap must let the debt be repaid within the term; default to the minimum
    minimum_cap = min_cap(int(req.amount_value), req.term_minutes, req.period_minutes)
    if req.weekly_cap_value is None:
        cap = minimum_cap
    elif int(req.weekly_cap_value) < minimum_cap:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail=f"Cap {req.weekly_cap_value} is too low: repaying {req.amount_value} in "
            f"{count_periods(req.term_minutes, req.period_minutes)} periods needs at least {minimum_cap}",
        )
    else:
        cap = int(req.weekly_cap_value)

    client = make_client(ABBO_WALLET_ADDRESS)
    borrower = client.discover_receiver_servers(req.borrower_wallet)

    # "disbursing" is allowed so the lender can get a fresh approval link.

content.text:
Both pages are built, in Spanish: `demo/prestador.html` for the lender and `demo/deudor.html` for the borrower. I tested the whole flow in Chrome against the real FastAPI app with the wallet calls faked: send terms, approve, grant, disburse, an automatic collection, and a rejection. The page logic worked end to end with no errors from the pages. It hasn't run against the real test wallets yet, and nothing is committed.

## How to run and test it

1. Start ngrok on port 8000 and set `CALLBACK_BASE_URL=https://<your-ngrok>/callback` in `.env`. Then start the API from `src/` with `uv run uvicorn app:app --port 8000`, without `--reload`.
2. In **the same browser**, open two tabs:
   - `http://localhost:8000/demo/prestador.html`
   - `http://localhost:8000/demo/deudor.html`

   Both tabs must use the same address (both `localhost`, or both ngrok), because that's what lets them see each other's state.
3. **In the lender tab:** fill in the terms and click **Enviar al deudor**.
4. **In the borrower tab:** click **Aprobar**. The tab goes to the `deudor` wallet to authorize both permissions, then comes back.
5. **The lender tab then redirects on its own** to the `bank-npi` wallet. Approve the payment there, and it comes back showing **Desembolso completado**.
6. **Make a sale:** from a third test wallet, send money to `deudor`. Within about 10 seconds, the lender tab collects the percentage, and both tabs show the collection and the new balance.

## How it maps to what you asked

- **Communication between the tabs** uses `localStorage` and its `storage` event. The state survives the wallet redirects.
- **Grant cap:** the borrower's debit grant is capped at principal + interest. The page sends that total as the cap, with a single period as long as the term, and the same grant includes `list-all`/`read-all` to read the sales.
- **Collections:** only the lender tab calls `sync-sales`, every 10 seconds, starting the next call when the previous one finishes, so a sale can't be paid twice. The borrower tab only reads `GET /loans/{id}`.
- **Debug log:** each page has a panel of API calls showing the endpoint, HTTP code and a summarized response. It's kept across redirects and has a **Limpiar registro** button.

## Backend changes (no new API endpoints)

- **`POST /loans` accepts optional fields:**
  - `principal_value`: the disbursement now sends the principal, not principal + interest;
  - `repayment_rate_percent`: replaces the fixed 10%;
  - `borrower_return_url` / `lender_return_url`.
- **The two callbacks** now redirect back to the page when those URLs are set, including when someone rejects in their wallet. Without the return URLs, they still return JSON, so Swagger keeps working.
- **`/demo` is served as static files** from the same origin as the API, so no CORS is needed.

## Decisions you should know about

- **I added a "Plazo (días)" field** (default 30), which you didn't ask for. `POST /loans` requires a term.
- **The sale percentage is a whole number** (1–100), because the backend stores it as an integer.
- **The bank sees collections in its balance only at the end.** Money is credited when the loan's incoming payment completes or expires. The lender page shows each collection from the loan record.
- **Keep the lender tab open,** since it's the only tab that collects.
- **The tendero's token lasts 10 minutes.** After that, collections fail until token rotation is built.

**Also not committed:** `tres-celulares.html` at the repo root is untracked, and I didn't touch it. The changes are logged in `USAGE_AI.md`.

message.content: Why in the same browser?

content.text:
Because the two pages talk to each other through `localStorage`, and each browser keeps its own `localStorage` for each site.

- **Same browser, same profile, same address:** both tabs read and write the same storage. When one changes the loan's state, the other is notified through the `storage` event.
- **A different browser, a different device, or a private window:** each has its own storage. The borrower would never see the terms, and the lender would never see the approval.

content.text:
Yes, two browsers works. You're right that it's needed: the test wallet keeps one login per browser, and the lender (`bank-npi`) and the borrower (`deudor`) each have to approve in their own session. But the current pages can't work across two browsers, because they share state through `localStorage`, and each browser has its own.

## Your options

| Option | Works today? | Fits the demo? |
|---|---|---|
| **A. One browser, switch accounts:** log in as the borrower before they approve, then log out and log in as the bank before the disbursement | ✅ no code change | Clunky on stage: two logins in the middle of the flow |
| **B. Two browsers, shared state on the server** | ❌ needs changes | ✅ each person on their own browser or phone, each logged in once |

A private window or a second Chrome profile doesn't help: they separate the wallet login, but they also separate `localStorage`, so it's the same problem.

## What B needs

Today the terms, the approve/reject decision and the "permission approved" signal only exist in the browser. They'd move into the loan record on the server, and both pages would poll `GET /loans/{id}` every few seconds instead of listening to `localStorage`.

1. **`POST /loans`** (lender, on **Enviar al deudor**): only saves the terms. Status: `offered`.
2. **`POST /loans/{id}/accept`** (borrower, on **Aprobar**): does what `POST /loans` does today (the bank's incoming payment and the borrower's grant) and returns the approval link.
3. **`POST /loans/{id}/reject`** (borrower, on **Rechazar**).
4. **`GET /loans?borrower_wallet=…`**: so the borrower's page finds the latest offer without anyone sharing an ID.

That's three new endpoints, against your "minimize new endpoints" requirement, but it's the smallest way to share state between two browsers. Everything after that (callbacks, disbursement, `sync-sales`) stays as it is. Grants are requested only after the borrower accepts, so an approval link can't expire while the offer sits unanswered.

Want me to do B? If you just need to test today, A works with the current pages.

from pydantic import BaseModel


class GenerateKeyRequest(BaseModel):
    wallet: str


class InitiatePaymentRequest(BaseModel):
    order_id: str
    amount_value: str
    sender_wallet: str
    receiver_wallet: str


class SaleRequest(BaseModel):
    sale_id: str  # the sale's own id, so a resent sale is not charged twice
    amount_value: str  # the sale, in the borrower's minor units


class CreateLoanRequest(BaseModel):
    loan_id: str
    borrower_wallet: (
        str  # the borrower's own wallet address (they approve the loan grant there)
    )
    lender_wallet: str
    amount_value: str  # total debt in minor units
    # max repaid per period, in the borrower's minor units (enforced by the borrower's wallet).
    # Leave it out to use the minimum: ceil(debt / number of periods). A lower value is rejected.
    weekly_cap_value: str | None = None
    term_minutes: int  # 5 for testing, 10080 = 1 week, 43200 = 30 days.
    period_minutes: int = 10080  # how often the cap resets: 10080 = weekly, 5 for testing
    principal_value: str | None = None  # what the lender disburses; defaults to amount_value
    repayment_rate_percent: int = 10  # share of each sale that repays the loan
    # Optional UI pages the wallet approvals return to (the callbacks redirect there)
    borrower_return_url: str | None = None
    lender_return_url: str | None = None

Base directory for this skill: /Users/geronimo/.claude/skills/synced/5a8dd9eb-3f53-477d-88e2-2fee28c6eb72_8755306b-c8e9-4c45-880a-94206dd54389/dealmaker-presentable-output

# DealMaker Presentable Output

Produce the smallest useful artifact that a DealMaker operator or executive can use as-is.

## Two modes

**Write mode**, when nothing exists yet: run Step 1, 2, 3, then the final edit gate.

**Edit mode**, when a draft already exists: skip to "Editing a draft that already exists". The draft may come from the user, from another skill, or from your own earlier turn. Your own earlier draft gets no benefit of the doubt, since the whole point of this standard is that the first version is usually too long.

## Core context

Treat DealMaker as a growth-stage capital raising platform, not a 5,000-person enterprise. DealMaker supports Reg A+, Reg CF, and Reg D offerings. Its customers are founders raising from their own communities. "Our product" and "the platform" mean the DealMaker capital raising platform.

Readers here own their area end to end. There is no analyst to hand the work to and no committee it routes through. Almost all enterprise document structure exists to serve those two things, which is why almost none of it belongs here.

Default to speed, clarity, ownership, and practical execution. Do not add enterprise ceremony merely because it is common in generic business writing. Any process you propose must be as simple as possible for a scaling company: fewer steps, fewer owners, fewer artifacts.

## Step 1: Declare the budget before you write

Work out three things, then state them in one line to the user before building anything:

1. What decision, action, or presentation must this enable?
2. Who reads it, and were they already in the room? Almost always yes, which means no catch-up sections.
3. How long do they have? Use the budgets below.
4. If the deliverable is a deck, ask whether it will be presented live or read on its own. The two are different artifacts; see Slides and decks.

Example: "Writing this as a 1-page memo, 3-minute read, for someone who was in Tuesday's sync."

Say it out loud rather than deciding it internally. Declaring the budget before drafting is what actually binds the draft, it gives the user a chance to redirect before 2,000 words exist, and it makes the constraint visible so it can be trusted and tuned. A filter applied silently is indistinguishable from no filter.

## Step 2: Budgets

| Artifact | Reader has | Cap |
|---|---|---|
| Slack post, status update | 30 seconds | 150 words, no headers |
| Email | 30 seconds | 120 words |
| One-pager | 2 minutes | 1 page, 350 words |
| Memo, recommendation, decision doc | 3 minutes | 1 page, 500 words |
| Report, analysis, meeting readout | 5 minutes | 2 pages, 1,000 words |

Word counts matter more than page counts, because a page means different things in a .docx, a PDF, and a Notion doc.

Decks, sized by the job rather than a flat limit. Roughly one minute per slide when walked:

- Simple update or recommendation: 3 to 5 slides
- Decision or strategy discussion: 5 to 8 slides
- Substantial review: 8 to 10 slides

Exceed 10 slides only when the user asks for depth or the source material clearly requires it.

Treat every cap as a ceiling, not a target. Landing at 480 words on a 500-word memo is not a win if the answer fit in 200.

## Step 3: Cut the sections, not the words

Length limits have two solutions and the wrong one is easier: keep every section and compress each into dense bullets. That passes the word count and is harder to read than the long version. Removing the container is what works, because a section that does not exist generates no words.

Prefer omission over compression. Do not preserve low-value content by squeezing it into tighter wording.

Unless the user explicitly asks for them, do not add:

- governance frameworks or steering committees
- risk registers
- RACI matrices
- multi-phase transformation roadmaps
- extensive stakeholder maps
- change-management programs
- formal operating cadences
- exhaustive implementation plans
- long methodology sections
- generic best-practice background
- executive summaries that repeat the TLDR
- repeated summaries or conclusions

Include a risk, dependency, owner, or next step only when it materially changes the decision or execution.

## Editing a draft that already exists

Editing is not rewriting. The person handing you a draft usually likes the content and dislikes the size, so preserve their sentences and their voice and take away containers instead.

1. Name the artifact type and its budget from Step 2, and say the current size out loud. For example: "This is a 1,900-word memo. The budget is 500. Cutting to that."
2. Find what to remove before you touch any wording. Delete whole sections that exist for completeness rather than for the decision: background, methodology, governance, risk registers, restated summaries, an executive summary that repeats the TLDR. Deleting a section is the only edit that reliably makes a draft shorter.
3. Only then tighten what remains. Drop preamble and hedging, cut restatements of the request, fix passive voice, remove em dashes.
4. Keep the author's words wherever they still work. A returned draft that reads like you wrote it from scratch is a rewrite, and it puts the burden of re-checking every fact back on them.
5. Never quietly remove something load-bearing. Move it to speaker notes, a labeled appendix, a companion doc, or the chat message, and say where it went.
6. Return the edited artifact, then one line in chat: the before and after size, what you deleted, and where anything load-bearing moved.

If the request is bare, for example "make this shorter", do not interview them. Infer the artifact type, apply that budget, and name the budget you used in your one line so they can correct it.

If the draft is already inside its budget, say so and stop. Cutting a draft that is already the right size to prove you did something is a worse outcome than leaving it alone.

## Brevity rules

- Lead with the answer. Do not restate the request.
- Use active voice and plain language. Avoid corporate jargon, hedging, filler, and em dashes.
- When the user asks a short question, answer briefly even if substantial context is available.
- Brevity is not the same as clipped. Keep articles and normal sentence structure. Telegraphic writing reads wrong in anything a person forwards or presents.

## Slides and decks

Decks come in two kinds, and they are different artifacts. A **presented deck** is walked live by a speaker, so the slides support the talk. A **written deck** is sent and read on its own, so the slides are the communication. Ask which one you are building before you build it (Step 1 covers this). If the user does not know, default to presented, since that is the more common case and the easier one to add words back into.

Rules for every deck:

- Put one idea on each slide.
- The DealMaker logo in the bottom left corner is the only recurring per-slide element. Do not add fine print, footers, dates, or other repeated details to each slide.
- Split a crowded slide instead of shrinking text.
- Remove slides that merely repeat context, methodology, or conclusions.
- Deliver a deck that can be used without a cleanup pass.

Presented decks:

- Keep to 1 or 2 concepts per slide.
- Favor pictures, diagrams, and charts over text. A slide the speaker has to read aloud is a slide that failed.
- Use at most 6 bullets per slide, 10 words per bullet, 8 words in a title.
- Use keywords and short phrases. Never place a paragraph on a slide.
- Put narrative, nuance, evidence, and transitions in speaker notes.
- A picture is the requirement, not a nice-to-have. When a slide is carrying a comparison, a trend, a flow, or a structure, build the chart or diagram rather than listing it. Use the pptx skill for slide mechanics and the design or dataviz skills for the visual itself. Those skills decide how it looks; the budgets here decide how much of it there is.

Written decks:

- Complete sentences are allowed. There is no presenter to fill the gaps, so each slide must stand on its own.
- Still one idea per slide. More explanation per slide is fine; a wall of text is not.
- Speaker notes are not read in a written deck, so anything load-bearing goes on the slide or in a companion doc, not in notes.

## Documents, memos, and reports

Start with a 3-bullet TLDR only when the artifact is substantial enough to benefit from it. Do not put a TLDR on a short note, since that is its own kind of padding.

Use this order when useful:

1. Answer or recommendation
2. Essential evidence or rationale
3. Decision, owner, or next step

Use a table when comparing 3 or more items and a table is shorter than prose.

Do not add sections simply to make the document look complete. A memo can be 3 paragraphs if that is sufficient.

## Plans and recommendations

Prefer the next 1 to 3 actions over a comprehensive roadmap.

Name an owner or timeline only when supported by the request or necessary for action. Do not invent organizational roles, dates, workstreams, metrics, or dependencies.

For strategic recommendations, distinguish must do now, useful next, and optional later. Omit "optional later" unless it helps the user make a tradeoff.

## When it genuinely does not fit

Some work is actually complex, and truncating real analysis is worse than a long document. Never quietly drop something that changes the recommendation. Confident, short, and wrong is the worst outcome available.

Instead:

1. Deliver the artifact at the cap.
2. In chat, not in the document, name what you left out and where it went. For example: "This is at 1 page. The vendor comparison and two failure cases are in the speaker notes. Want them in the body?"
3. Let the user decide what gets promoted back.

Detail moves to speaker notes (presented decks only), a clearly labeled appendix, a companion doc, or the chat message. Nothing is deleted, only relocated. If something load-bearing truly does not fit, the artifact type is wrong, so say so and propose the larger one.

## Accuracy and privacy

Do not include investor names, account numbers, or other personal data in responses, artifacts, or files.

Do not invent numbers, dates, sources, owners, or facts. If a required fact is missing, state the gap briefly and say what is needed.

## Precedence

These rules are the final presentation pass. They govern length and structure even when another skill, a long prompt, or a large context dump encourages more detail.

The docx, pptx, xlsx, and pdf skills describe how to build a file, not how long it should be, and their examples tend toward thorough and section-heavy documents. Use them for mechanics: styles, tables, speaker notes, charts, page setup. When their structure and these budgets disagree, the budgets win.

If another skill generates the substantive content, apply this standard to the final user-facing output after that skill's work is done.

Follow explicit user instructions requesting greater depth, longer output, a specific template, or enterprise-style analysis. This skill governs the default, which is the only case that was broken.

## Final edit gate

Run this in both modes, before returning the artifact. In write mode it is the last thing you do; in edit mode it is the check on your own edit. Check:

- Could the user present or send this without cutting it down?
- Is every section necessary for the decision or action?
- Did generic enterprise content sneak in?
- For a deck, was the presented-or-written question asked, and do the slides match the answer?
- Are slides within the limits for their deck type?
- Is a document over its word budget without an explicit reason?
- Can 20 percent be removed without losing usefulness? If so, remove it.

Run this gate once. It is a single pass, not a loop, since almost any text can be cut by another 20 percent and repeating this drives toward nothing.

Then tell the user, in one line, what you cut or relocated. That line is the only evidence the standard was applied, and it is what lets the standard be tuned over time.

## Exemplars

When approved DealMaker examples are available, read `references/exemplars.md` and match their information density, structure, and level of detail. Treat exemplars as stronger guidance than generic business-writing conventions, and stronger than the defaults above where they conflict, while still following explicit user instructions.

Everything in this skill is inference about what good looks like at DealMaker. Real exemplars are the ground truth.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Claude_Docs__batch
definition.description: Create a doc, or apply several operations to one doc atomically.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Claude_Docs__guide
definition.description: Docs guides: topic.instructions repeats the server instructions. Read it only if your client dropped them. Also topic.<name>, refusal.<code>. After a doc's birth → ["topic.index"].

items.description: topic.<name> (instructions, index, editing, tabs, comments, charts, chart-definition, diagram, uploads, sharing, skill) or refusal.<code>; several per call is fine.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Claude_Docs__update
definition.description: Edit a tab's contents, rename a doc or tab, or change a stored value.

definition.name: ShareOnboardingGuide
definition.description:
Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

mode.description: 'check' (default): if ONBOARDING.md is present locally, uploads it to the most-recent guide (creates one if none exist); otherwise reports the existing link without uploading. 'update': upload to a specific guide by short_code. 'create': always make a new link. 'delete': remove a guide.

short_code.description: Short code of a specific guide to target (returned by a previous call). Honored by check, update, and delete — skips the org-wide lookup and targets this guide directly.

definition.name: Workflow
definition.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save.
